---
title: "OHI regions — land and marine, 1 km"
output:
  html_document:
    toc: true
    toc_float: true
---

This raster gives every 1 km cell in an OHI region a region number from 1 to 9.
Land and marine of the same region share that number. Region 1 is 1 on the
peninsula and 1 on the water, and the same is true through Region 9.

The grid is the marine region raster: Mexico ITRF2008 / LCC (EPSG:6372),
1 km cells, and the same extent and origin. A cell that already has a marine
region number keeps it. A cell that the marine raster leaves empty is filled
when its center falls inside a land polygon, using that polygon's region
number. Cells outside all nine regions stay empty.

The lookup table has one row per region: the number stored in the raster, the
region name, the state, and the ecoregion. Land and marine of a region share
those names. The table also records how many square kilometres of each region
are marine and how many were filled from the land polygons.

```{r setup}
library(tidyverse)
library(terra)
library(sf)
library(knitr)
library(writexl)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)

marine_path <- "/home/frazier/ohi_goc_prep/spatial/ohi_regions/ohi_marine_raster_1km.tif"
region_path <- "/home/frazier/ohi_goc_prep/spatial/ohi_regions/goc_ohi_rgns.shp"
out_dir <- "/home/frazier/ohi_goc_prep/spatial/marine_land_raster"
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## 1. The marine grid

Cell values in this raster are already the marine region numbers 1–9. Land and
water outside the nine marine regions are empty. The combined raster is built
on this object, so the two files share resolution, CRS, extent, and origin.

```{r template}
marine <- rast(marine_path)
names(marine) <- "marine_id"

cat(
  "CRS:", crs(marine, describe = TRUE)$code, "\n",
  "Resolution, m:", paste(res(marine), collapse = " × "), "\n",
  "Rows × columns:", paste(dim(marine)[1:2], collapse = " × "), "\n",
  "Marine cells:", as.numeric(global(!is.na(marine), "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]), "\n"
)
```

## 2. Land polygons on the same grid

Land polygons carry the same `Region_1`–`Region_9` names as the marine
polygons. The number written into a land cell is that region number. Rasterizing
uses the cell center, which is the rule used for the marine raster. A land
value is kept only where the marine raster is empty, so the marine numbers do
not move.

```{r land}
regions <- st_read(region_path, quiet = TRUE) %>%
  st_make_valid() %>%
  st_transform(crs(marine))

land <- regions %>%
  filter(location == "land") %>%
  mutate(rgn_num = as.integer(str_remove(rgn_id, "Region_")))

stopifnot(sort(unique(land$rgn_num)) == 1:9)

# Cell center inside a land polygon. Empty where the center is not on land.
land_id <- rasterize(vect(land), marine, field = "rgn_num", background = NA)
names(land_id) <- "land_id"

combined <- ifel(!is.na(marine), marine, land_id)
names(combined) <- "rgn_id"

# Every marine cell keeps the value from the marine raster.
marine_unchanged <- ifel(is.na(marine), 1, ifel(combined == marine, 1, 0))
stopifnot(as.numeric(global(marine_unchanged, "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]) == ncell(marine))
stopifnot(compareGeom(combined, marine, stopOnError = FALSE))
```

## 3. Region lookup

One row per region number. `marine_km2` counts cells that were already in the
marine raster. `land_km2` counts cells filled from the land polygons. Each
1 km cell is 1 km².

```{r lookup}
region_info <- regions %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(location == "marine") %>%
  transmute(
    id = as.integer(id),
    rgn_id = rgn_id,
    estado = estado,
    ecorgn = ecorgn,
    region_label = paste(
      rgn_id,
      str_replace_all(estado, "_", " "),
      str_replace_all(ecorgn, "_", " "),
      sep = " · "
    )
  ) %>%
  arrange(id)

# Land contribution: combined id where the marine raster was empty.
land_cells <- ifel(is.na(marine), combined, NA)
area_cells <- c(marine, land_cells)
names(area_cells) <- c("marine_id", "land_id")

area_by_id <- as.data.frame(area_cells, na.rm = FALSE) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "part", values_to = "id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(id)) %>%
  count(id, part, name = "km2") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = part, values_from = km2, values_fill = 0) %>%
  rename(marine_km2 = marine_id, land_km2 = land_id)

region_table <- region_info %>%
  left_join(area_by_id, by = "id") %>%
  mutate(
    marine_km2 = replace_na(marine_km2, 0),
    land_km2 = replace_na(land_km2, 0),
    total_km2 = marine_km2 + land_km2
  )

kable(
  region_table %>%
    select(id, rgn_id, estado, ecorgn, marine_km2, land_km2, total_km2),
  digits = 0,
  col.names = c("Raster id", "Region", "State", "Ecoregion", "Marine, km²", "Land, km²", "Total, km²"),
  caption = "Region attributes for the land-and-marine raster. The raster id is the same on land and on the water."
)

write_csv(region_table, file.path(out_dir, "ohi_regions_land_marine.csv"))
write_xlsx(region_table, file.path(out_dir, "ohi_regions_land_marine.xlsx"))
```

## 4. Map

Each color is one region, on land and on the water.

```{r map-data}
rgn_colors <- c(
  "Region 1" = "#C03729",
  "Region 2" = "#E68C7C",
  "Region 3" = "#FC8F24",
  "Region 4" = "#dcaa38",
  "Region 5" = "#cbd2a0",
  "Region 6" = "#98a25a",
  "Region 7" = "#747428",
  "Region 8" = "#627391",
  "Region 9" = "#8d61a9"
)

map_df <- as.data.frame(combined, xy = TRUE, na.rm = TRUE)
names(map_df)[3] <- "id"
map_df <- map_df %>%
  left_join(region_info %>% select(id, rgn_id), by = "id") %>%
  mutate(
    region_label = factor(
      str_replace(rgn_id, "_", " "),
      levels = names(rgn_colors)
    )
  )
```

```{r plot-regions, fig.width=8, fig.height=9}
region_plot <- ggplot(map_df, aes(x, y, fill = region_label)) +
  geom_raster() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = rgn_colors, name = NULL) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    title = "OHI regions, land and marine",
    subtitle = "1 km cells. Land and marine of a region share one id.",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank())

print(region_plot)
ggsave(
  file.path(out_dir, "ohi_land_marine_regions_1km.png"),
  region_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 9,
  dpi = 150,
  bg = "white"
)
```

## 5. Saved raster

Values are the region numbers 1–9. Empty cells are outside the nine regions.
Where the marine raster has a value, this raster has the same value.

```{r save}
raster_path <- file.path(out_dir, "ohi_land_marine_raster_1km.tif")
writeRaster(combined, raster_path, overwrite = TRUE, datatype = "INT1U", NAflag = 255)

cat("Raster:", raster_path, "\n")
cat("Lookup:", file.path(out_dir, "ohi_regions_land_marine.xlsx"), "\n")
cat("File, KB:", round(file.size(raster_path) / 1024), "\n")
cat(
  "Cells with a region id:",
  as.numeric(global(!is.na(combined), "sum", na.rm = TRUE)[1, 1]), "\n"
)
```

The raster is `r raster_path`.
